label: input d at step 0 or 1
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the letter d at the first or second original step (t=0 or t=1). Dev P=R=1.0. Magnitude is set by position: d at t=0 always gives the max activation (~2.38) and carries ~84% of mass; d at t=1 fires weakly (~0.39-0.56, ~16-24% of max), with the exact value depending on the preceding token (e.g. after q ~0.56, after d ~0.43, after x ~0.39). Never fires on d at t>=2, on any other token, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase (including when d is being output or fed back).

issues: No refutation found. On the test split the predicate (in_tok == tok("d")) & (t <= 1) scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 (n_active = n_predicted = 33598), and misses lists 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The dev profile backs every factual claim. Activation is 0 in the delimiter and copy phases, and 0 at t>=2. All of it falls on in_tok d. t=0 carries 0.842 of the activation mass and t=1 carries 0.158. Top examples are d at t=0 with activation 1.00 relative to max (2.377).

The t=1 magnitudes depend on the previous token as claimed. After q the d fires at about 0.23 relative (0.56), after d at 0.18 (0.43), after x at 0.16 (0.39), and after u/o about 0.17-0.18. This matches the stated 0.39-0.56 range.
Minor caveat: 'always max' at t=0 rests on the top examples and the mass share; no other test of it was run. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
